Glad you have a published build that can replicate this -- i agree that "lots of time played" seems to be a relevant factor, when I opened the other ticket i tried in a variety of ways to compel it to crash and failed, but _certain_ players can semi-reliably trigger it with a couple hours of play, both on windows I believe, though one plays sometimes on steam deck and I'm not totally sure what device they're on when the crashes hit.

spawning thousands of objects doesn't seem to do it, spawning them in a thread doesn't seem to do it. The bug also makes it relatively figure out to happen exactly what was going on before the crash, although I do feel like cases where objects were instantiated in threads exacerbated the issue

> spawning thousands of objects doesn't seem to do it, spawning them in a thread doesn't seem to do it. 

Yes, that's exactly our experience as well: there's never been a report about a problem during gameplay when this happens. And we instantiate plenty of graphics scenes during gameplay as AI entities spawn. So for some reason it seems the scene load failure only happens when a major new game scene is loaded (the graphics scenes for entities are relatively much more simple than the new major game scene that is loaded when the game swaps scenes).

>  The bug also makes it relatively figure out to happen exactly what was going on before the crash

I think there's a missing word here? Relatively what?

> > The bug also makes it relatively figure out to happen exactly what was going on before the crash
> 
> I think there's a missing word here? Relatively what?

Sorry yeah -- `relatively difficult to figure out`.

 Since the crash happens in the C++ part, all there is to go on is the trace which lets you know what function it happened in, but then it can be unclear as to which node is causing the problem, and you can't (to the best of my knowledge) catch the exception in c# to try and log what it was you were _trying_ to do at the time. So then you can try logging literally everything, but since it usually takes 2+ hours of play  before the bug shows up, that creates fairly bulky log files to work with.

Actually there seems to be a relevant thread about this here: https://forum.godotengine.org/t/random-failure-to-load-packedscenes/67830/3

>  I have two builds now, one works and one doesn’t. I made tiny inconsequential code changes to perturb two different outputs with no meaningful differences. The only binary difference in the whole app is in my game dll and game pdb. The only semantic difference, per dotPeek, is the perturbations I made. Nevertheless, one fails to reliably load packed scenes, and the other loads them reliably. Given there’s no meaningful semantic difference, I can only assume that there must be some difference in the binary layout somehow. On a binary diff of the two DLL’s, the differences are enormous. dotnet doesn’t seem to produce a very stable layout at all.
> 
> Nevertheless, that’s where I’m at. Something in the binary layout of the DLL is broken in random builds for no rhyme or reason.

Thanks for looking at this issue. A funny thing has happened a while ago... Thanks to the new log interceptor feature in Godot we can now show a popup window to the player the first time the engine has an error. And as a result the players seem to never see this error again. So my assumption by this point is that some slight memory corruption starts to show up and that eventually causes corruption of the packed scene cache or class DB.

The most common errors we now get reported are actually of the form (I included this because I saw your link to #83762 which has "handle" in the title):

```
exception: System.InvalidOperationException: Handle is not initialized.
   at Godot.Bridge.ScriptManagerBridge.SwapGCHandleForType(IntPtr oldGCHandlePtr, IntPtr* outNewGCHandlePtr, godot_bool createWeak)
```

And yes, that's the full callstack which makes trying to figure out anything in depth about this problem a bit difficult.

And: `exception: Condition "p_arrays.size() != ARRAY_MAX" is true.` which triggers when we are dynamically generating meshes.

So this specific error hasn't been seen for quite a while, likely because the start of the error conditions are now caught instead of the final symptom of being unable to continue playing. Both the handle not initialized and the mesh generation errors seem like they still allow the player to continue playing as they aren't immediately fatal, but due to good warning message most players make a save and restart the game at this point. That is my hunch at least why we haven't seen any reports about this problem for a while.

Just FYI I've also been seeing a lot of this error in Sentry. I have a game released on Steam and it seemed to happen randomly for longer play times. I was not able to reproduce it, seems to happen only for longer play-times and ones with a lot of churn. So it's definitely still live.

If there is anything I could provide let me know.

As an intermediate solution I've stopped loading dynamically entirely and just the scene once.

Game was released this month with `4.7.2`, so it's recent.

I'm getting similar problems in my demo that load a lot of scenes dynamically.
Moving to IgnoreDeep while loading the resources seem to have fixed the "Handle is not initialized" crashes:
var resource = ResourceLoader.Load(resourcePath, typeHint, ResourceLoader.CacheMode.IgnoreDeep);

So that this can eventually be fixed in Godot I installed Claude and had it analyze my source code and try to extract minimal repros of both the packed scene bug and the "Handle is not initialized" bug. A few iterations later it was actually successful 👍

It crashes reliably using AOT builds, but for any app running long enough it could happen even in regular release builds:
https://github.com/klootas/GodotGcRepro
